description.purpose: The container this member's assistants are instantiated into. It ships empty and open: no cells, no ports, no contract of its own. Its whole job is to be an address that already exists, so the mutation that instantiates an assistant has somewhere to put one -- and so the member can wire its holders and its CHANNELS to that address once instead of once per agent. Since GH #454 it is also where a turn is ADDRESSED: the channel stamps `context.assistant` with the name of the agent the person meant, and the per-assistant edges inside this container are what read it.
description.use_when: Never on its own -- it travels with member@1.9.2. Address it as <member>/assistants in the add_nodes of the mutation that instantiates an assistant, and draw that assistant's own edges in the same mutation. TRANSIT, derived from the contract of assistant@2.8.0 and from what this member sends back down (firewall@2.3.1, memory-hive@3.4.0) -- IN, six: the two a sibling of this container produces -- in_turn (the screened turn coming back from ./firewall on pass, carrying context.assistant) and in_bundle (the memory hive's answer) -- plus in_build_result, which enters at the member's own door and is forwarded here unchanged, because its producer sits four levels up, and, since member@1.9.0, in_delegation: a handover from a channel whose model answers on its own timeline, drawn from ./channels STRAIGHT to this container and never through ./firewall, whose exit stamps in_turn and would turn a handover into a turn of the conversation. Two more arrive from the member's HOLDERS rather than from one sibling: in_tool and in_menu, the tool_result and the tool_schemas that ./memory-hive, ./apps and ./channels send back to whichever generation asked for them -- they are stamped here and addressed on the permissive form of the guard, because a holder answering a call knows the call and not the caller (GH #552). The four an assistant ALSO accepts -- in_advice, in_sweep, in_prune, in_round_sweep -- are deliberately NOT lanes of the member (ruling W7-R5): their producer is ./cogny inside the assistant, a second agent standing beside it in this container, or an operator or timer, and each of those addresses <member>/assistants/<agent> at its own path. That is allowed because neither this level nor the assistant declares params.ports, so both are open and the port boundary refuses an outside endpoint only for a SEALED hive. A lane a level declares but nothing ever crosses it on is the mirror image of one it emits with no edge -- see templates/member/README.md. OUT, the eight an assistant emits: answer, write, turn_write, sidecar, recall, prune, error, build. extraction is GONE since talky@5.1.0 renamed the port (GH #607), and a rendered exit for it would be an edge nothing can travel. Four of them stop at this level -- answer at ./channels, recall and the sidecar's memory section at ./memory-hive, write additionally fanned onto ./memory-hive's close pass -- and `sidecar` is the newest of them (member@1.7.0, GH #607) and it is the one this container does not decide about at all: it is SORTED at the member, hop.section == 'memory' onto the memory hive's in_remember door and every other section into ./apps, so what leaves this container is one lane and what arrives at two different holders is one message per section. The memory section is the one that must not stop HERE, in the container: it is the write half of the member's memory (GH #122, ADR 0012), wired the way talky's own recipe prescribes, two edges and never one. The others are re-emitted by the member on its own contract and leave the level; the parent drains them. ADDRESSING is the one thing this container costs per assistant: one edge `./assistants -> ./assistants/<name>` per lane that arrives -- `in_turn` guarded on `context.assistant == '<name>'`, `in_tool` and `in_menu` on the permissive form of the same guard, and since member@1.9.0 `in_delegation` beside them on that same permissive form -- and `./assistants/<name> -> ./assistants` for each lane that leaves. A lane the member stamps onto this container and nobody carries one hop further dies HERE, as hive_no_route, which is what GH #803 measured on a built colony. The substrate resolves an edge target statically, so there is no way to write 'send it to whatever context.assistant names' as one edge -- a new assistant is a new pair of edges, and that is a rule rather than an accident. TWO of those lanes end DEEPER than the assistant since GH #562: the recall road is a v-lane (ADR-0020). `recall` leaves `./assistants/<name>/talky` and `./assistants/<name>/cogny` directly for this container's rim, carrying the `recall_caller` stamp, and `in_bundle` goes straight back down to the asker the token names -- four edges per assistant instead of the two that used to end at the generation's own path, each naming its lane. The permission is the generation's own contract (`at: ["./talky", "./cogny"]`) and nothing this container declares; what the container does is DRAW them, which is the same job it has always had. Nothing else about the road moved: the member's `./assistants -> ./memory-hive` door is still where `recall` becomes `in_query` and picks up the audience, the room and the as-of, and the member declares both lanes so no v-lane may skip that door.
description.not_in_scope: No ports, because a sealed hive refuses exactly the endpoints an assistant instantiation needs (hive_port_boundary). No slot: GH #285's slot governs an address that does not exist, and this container does exist, so the declared unbound word could never fire -- see unbound_slot_behaviour in crates/meclaw-colony/src/colony.rs, which steps aside as soon as the target is a registered hive scope. No params.contract either: this container is wired by the member the moment the member is instantiated, and a contracted hive whose declared lanes have no door or exit INSIDE it refuses every later mutation in the colony (mutation::hive_contract::check_lane_doors, via hive_path_is_wired). The transit list above is therefore prose the instantiating mutation reads, not a declaration the substrate would enforce against an empty container. No cells: what stands in this container is an assistant, and an assistant is instantiated, never shipped. And no address rule of its own beyond the per-assistant guards: which agent `context.assistant` names is decided by the channel that stamped it, and a channel that could not tell stamps its own default (GH #454). No model decides it.
